title: What happens during a gastroscopy?
intro: A gastroscopy is an examination in which a thin flexible tube with a camera is passed through the mouth to look at the gullet, stomach and first part of the small intestine. It helps find causes of pain, reflux, bleeding or swallowing problems, and takes about ten to twenty minutes.

sections.heading: Why it is done
paragraphs: Doctors use gastroscopy to investigate persistent heartburn, upper abdominal pain, difficulty swallowing, vomiting, anaemia or bleeding. It can show ulcers, inflammation, hernias, polyps, tumours and infections. During the exam, small tissue samples can be taken and some problems, like bleeding, can be treated.

sections.heading: Preparation
paragraphs: You need to stop eating about six hours and drinking about two hours before. Tell the doctor about blood thinners, diabetes, allergies and heart or lung conditions. If you are sedated, someone should take you home, and you must not drive for the rest of the day. Remove dentures.

sections.heading: During the procedure
paragraphs: You lie on your left side, and your throat may be numbed with a spray. Sedation is often given. A mouth guard protects the teeth. The tube is passed over the tongue, and you are asked to swallow. It does not block breathing. You may feel pressure, gagging or bloating from air that is introduced.

sections.heading: Afterwards
paragraphs: You rest for a while, and may feel bloated or have a sore throat for a day. Eat and drink when the throat numbness has passed. Seek help for severe abdominal or chest pain, fever, vomiting blood or black stools. Serious complications, such as a tear or bleeding, are rare.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: The doctor often gives the findings after the examination, although biopsy results take several days. Ask about treatment, follow-up and any changes to your medicines. A stomach bacterium called Helicobacter pylori can be found by biopsy and treated with antibiotics.

examples.title: Preparing the day before
examples.text: Imagine your gastroscopy is in the morning. You could fast after midnight, take only agreed medicines with a sip of water and arrange a lift home.

examples.title: Dealing with nerves
examples.text: Suppose you worry about gagging. You might ask about sedation and practise slow breathing.
